findings.rationale: WA's feature means move away from its round-1 baseline from round 11 on: per-round shift_sd jumps from near 0 (rounds 1-10, max 0.3288) to 0.3-0.56 in every round from 11 to 20. Its uploaded updates agree with the federation median in rounds 1-10 (cos 0.86-1.0) and then decorrelate from round 11 (cos 0.386 at round 11, 0.257 at 12, about 0 or negative afterwards). The drift summary independently gives onset 11. Round-20 feature screens also show WA's GenHlth and DiffWalk tails off from other clients. WA's local AUC and CITL are normal, consistent with a feature shift rather than label error. Its large update norm is consistent with its size (about 11k records), so I do not treat the norm as poisoning.

CO has the largest drift mean_shift_sd of any client (0.3464) and a max_shift_sd of 1.184 on HighBP, with drift onset at round 11 in the summary. Per-round shifts are large in later rounds (0.55 at round 9, 1.05 at round 18, 0.59 at round 19), well above the noise floor of mid-size clean clients. The round-20 feature screen independently shows CO's GenHlth mean well below the federation (noise-adjusted z -3.14) and its DiffWalk upper tail elevated (noise-adjusted z 3.39). Confidence is moderate because each feature deviation is only about 3 noise units. Local AUC and CITL are normal.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed leads with narrower queries. Two clients show consistent drift: WA (shift from round 11, with update directions decorrelating from the median at the same round) and CO (large later-round shifts and feature deviations, moderate confidence). Not reported: WA's large update norm (plausibly explained by its size); CA's later-round drift values (not confirmed by the round-20 feature screen); NC and ND single-feature tail/SD anomalies (isolated, not corroborated); and near-zero predicted-risk subgroup O/E outliers in small subgroups (likely noise artefacts). No evidence of poisoning, free-riding, label noise, prevalence shift, subgroup bias, missing-value sentinels or explanation instability in the other clients. Note: one attribution_churn call was made with epsilon 0 but still charged 1.0 of budget.
